subject.title: fix: active-memory recall fails with billing rejections on subscription-only Claude CLI setups

question: Should subscription-auth embedded helper dispatch remain a core-owned `claude-cli` special case and public eligibility API, or should Anthropic declare the capability through a provider-owned contract consumed by generic core dispatch?
rationale: Both shapes can fix the bug, but choosing the permanent provider-versus-core API boundary creates a compatibility commitment that cannot be inferred safely from tests or live proof.

options.title: Provider-owned capability
options.body: Move Claude subscription eligibility and billing policy into the Anthropic plugin while retaining generic dispatch, transcript, and grant machinery in core.

options.title: Approve core special case
options.body: Land the current core-owned `claude-cli` policy and explicitly accept the new Plugin SDK eligibility method as a supported compatibility surface.

options.title: Pause for broader helper routing
options.body: Hold this PR and design one shared contract with the remaining helper-routing work tracked at https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/57326.

recommendation.title: Provider-owned capability
recommendation.body: Move Claude subscription eligibility and billing policy into the Anthropic plugin while retaining generic dispatch, transcript, and grant machinery in core.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent plugin activation and provider-boundary work makes them the best available routing candidate for deciding this SDK ownership question.
